title: ADR-0128: VPC endpoints required for Redwood Private installer (AWS, alpha)
author: Victor Alvarez
body:
## Summary
Redwood Private (VPC) deployments must support a “private-only” mode (no public egress from workloads) to meet common enterprise controls. To make installs reproducible and supportable, the Private installer and reference Terraform modules will require a baseline set of AWS VPC endpoints (Gateway + Interface/PrivateLink), with a clearly documented “required vs optional” matrix.

This ADR defines:
- The minimum endpoints required for a successful install in private-only mode.
- Optional endpoints that improve operability and reduce support risk.
- Security guidance (endpoint policies, private DNS, and SG constraints).
- Installer preflight checks aligned to these requirements.

## Status
Published (alpha scope).

## Context / problem
Customer environments vary widely:
- Some allow NAT/public egress; others prohibit it entirely.
- Many require all control-plane and data-plane traffic to stay on private IPs.
- Install failures and “it works in our VPC but not yours” support cases frequently trace to missing endpoints or misconfigured private DNS.

The installer needs deterministic network reachability for:
- Pulling container images and Helm artifacts.
- Accessing AWS APIs from private subnets (including token vending / auth flows).
- Shipping logs to the configured destination.

If we do not specify a baseline endpoint set, we risk:
- Higher deployment variance and longer time-to-deploy.
- Repeated pilot/production failures due to missing endpoints (especially STS and ECR).
- Security regressions where customers open broad egress “temporarily” to unblock installs.

## Decision
For AWS VPC-based Redwood Private deployments targeting private-only egress (no outbound internet from private/isolated subnets), the following endpoint set is:

### Required endpoints (private-only mode)
These endpoints MUST be present when workloads do not have NAT/public egress.

1) **Amazon S3 – Gateway endpoint**
- Service: `com.amazonaws.<region>.s3`
- Type: Gateway (route table association)
- Why required:
  - ECR image layer retrieval uses S3 under the hood.
  - Installer artifacts and module-managed assets may be stored in S3 depending on configuration.
- Notes:
  - Must be associated to the route tables used by the subnets where cluster nodes / workloads run.

2) **Amazon ECR – Interface endpoints**
- Services:
  - `com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api`
  - `com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.dkr`
- Type: Interface (PrivateLink)
- Why required:
  - Cluster nodes and/or installer components must authenticate to ECR and pull images without internet access.
- Notes:
  - Requires **Private DNS enabled** for the endpoints in the default module pattern.
  - Security groups must allow HTTPS (443) from workload subnets to the endpoint ENIs.

3) **AWS STS – Interface endpoint**
- Service: `com.amazonaws.<region>.sts`
- Type: Interface
- Why required:
  - Required for role assumption and credential vending patterns commonly used by:
    - Kubernetes nodes using instance profiles
    - IRSA/web identity flows (when present)
    - Installer components using `AssumeRole` into a deployment role
  - Pilot installs have failed in “no egress” environments specifically due to missing STS reachability.
- Notes:
  - Requires Private DNS enabled in the default pattern to avoid hard-coded public STS endpoints.

4) **CloudWatch Logs – Interface endpoint (conditionally required)**
- Service: `com.amazonaws.<region>.logs`
- Type: Interface
- Required when:
  - The deployment config uses CloudWatch Logs as a sink for installer/runtime logs; OR
  - The reference architecture requires CW Logs for day-0 validation/troubleshooting in alpha.
- Why required:
  - Without it, logs can be black-holed in private-only environments, significantly increasing MTTR.

**Alpha policy:** For alpha “reference module” deployments, CloudWatch Logs endpoint is treated as **required by default** unless the customer explicitly configures an alternate log sink and acknowledges reduced supportability during initial bring-up.

### Optional (recommended) endpoints
These endpoints are not strictly required to complete an install in every topology, but they reduce operational risk and support burden.

1) **AWS Systems Manager (SSM) – Interface endpoints**
- Services:
  - `com.amazonaws.<region>.ssm`
  - `com.amazonaws.<region>.ssmmessages`
  - `com.amazonaws.<region>.ec2messages`
- Why recommended:
  - Enables private connectivity for troubleshooting workflows where customers use SSM Session Manager instead of SSH/bastions.
  - Reduces pressure to allow inbound admin access.
- Notes:
  - Particularly recommended for regulated environments.

2) **AWS KMS – Interface endpoint** (recommended when customer uses KMS and blocks egress)
- Service: `com.amazonaws.<region>.kms`
- Why recommended:
  - Supports KMS API calls from private workloads (encryption at rest integrations, envelope encryption, etc.).
- Alpha note:
  - Not required for the Terraform VPC foundation itself, but frequently required for customer platform standards.

3) **Amazon EC2 – Interface endpoint** (situational)
- Service: `com.amazonaws.<region>.ec2`
- Why recommended:
  - Some cluster bootstrapping and discovery tooling in customer environments calls EC2 APIs from within private subnets.
- Alpha note:
  - Do not require globally; enable as a toggle.

### Explicitly out of scope / not required by the installer (alpha)
- Full coverage for every AWS API used by every possible customer add-on.
- Automatic creation of endpoints for third-party SaaS integrations.
- Opinionated NACL rules (SG-based enforcement is the default; NACL guidance is documented separately).

## Endpoint matrix (alpha)
| Endpoint | Type | Default in reference modules | Installer preflight check | Rationale |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| S3 (`s3`) | Gateway | Yes | Yes | Required for ECR layer distribution and private artifact access |
| ECR API (`ecr.api`) | Interface | Yes | Yes | Required to auth to ECR without internet |
| ECR DKR (`ecr.dkr`) | Interface | Yes | Yes | Required to pull images without internet |
| STS (`sts`) | Interface | Yes | Yes | Required for role assumption / auth flows in private-only |
| CloudWatch Logs (`logs`) | Interface | Yes (default) | Yes (if CW Logs selected) | Restores observability in private-only environments |
| SSM suite (`ssm`, `ssmmessages`, `ec2messages`) | Interface | No (toggle) | No | Strongly recommended for secure admin access |
| KMS (`kms`) | Interface | No (toggle) | No | Recommended when customer requires KMS and blocks egress |

## Rationale / design notes
### Why S3 is a gateway endpoint (not interface)
- Gateway endpoint is simpler, cheaper, and avoids per-AZ ENI scaling concerns.
- It integrates via route tables, aligning with common “no NAT” patterns.

### Why ECR + STS are required even if the customer “has S3”
- ECR authentication and image pulls require ECR endpoints, and most auth flows require STS.
- The most common private-only failure mode is: customer adds S3 endpoint, but not ECR and STS.

### Private DNS guidance
Default module behavior for interface endpoints:
- **Enable Private DNS** for `ecr.api`, `ecr.dkr`, `sts`, and (when used) `logs`.
- If a customer disables Private DNS, they MUST provide an alternate DNS strategy (e.g., Route 53 private hosted zones or custom resolver rules) and accept that Redwood support may request re-enabling Private DNS during troubleshooting.

### Endpoint policies
- Reference modules will include endpoint policy stubs (deny-by-default templates) with safe defaults.
- Security baseline:
  - For S3 gateway endpoint policy: allow access to only the required buckets where feasible (customer-provided), otherwise allow `s3:GetObject`/`ListBucket` with documented tightening steps.
  - For interface endpoints: use security groups as the primary control; optionally add endpoint policies where supported.

### Security group constraints (interface endpoints)
- Endpoint ENIs should be placed in dedicated “endpoints” subnets or in private subnets per the selected topology.
- Endpoint SG:
  - Inbound: allow TCP/443 only from Redwood workload subnets / installer subnets.
  - Outbound: default allow (AWS-managed service); do not open broad egress from workloads.

## Alternatives considered
1) **Require NAT for alpha**
- Rejected: conflicts with enterprise “no public egress” requirements and creates security exceptions early.

2) **Make endpoints fully optional and document “common pitfalls”**
- Rejected: increases deployment variance and support burden; preflight checks become non-deterministic.

3) **Require a larger set of endpoints (EC2, EKS, Autoscaling, KMS, etc.) by default**
- Rejected for alpha: increases surface area, cost, and review time; we will add endpoints as evidence shows they are needed for the installer path.

## Consequences
### Positive
- Reliable private-only installs without broad egress.
- Clear preflight validation with actionable errors.
- Reduced pilot friction and faster time-to-deploy.

### Negative / trade-offs
- Additional AWS resources and per-hour costs for interface endpoints.
- More complex DNS and SG rules (especially in shared networking environments).
- Customers with centralized egress/proxy architectures may need explicit toggles and documentation to avoid “double plumbing.”

## Implementation notes (Terraform modules + installer)
### Terraform module requirements
- `modules/vpc-endpoints` must support:
  - Conditional creation per service.
  - Private DNS toggle per interface endpoint.
  - Endpoint SG creation with least-privilege defaults.
  - Route table associations for S3 gateway endpoint.
- Outputs required by installer integration:
  - VPC endpoint IDs per service
  - Private DNS enabled flag(s)
  - Subnet IDs where endpoints are placed (for troubleshooting)

### Installer preflight checks (minimum)
Installer must fail fast with clear guidance when in private-only mode:
- Resolve DNS and verify HTTPS reachability for:
  - `api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com`
  - `<account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com`
  - `sts.<region>.amazonaws.com`
- Validate that S3 is reachable via gateway routing (e.g., a simple S3 list/read against a known bucket if configured, or a generic connectivity check when not).
- If CloudWatch Logs is configured:
  - Verify `logs.<region>.amazonaws.com` reachability.

## Rollout / migration
- Alpha reference modules: enable required endpoints by default.
- Existing VPC adoption mode:
  - Installer will accept “bring-your-own endpoint IDs” and will still run reachability checks.
- Documentation must include:
  - A “private-only checklist” with the required endpoints.
  - A troubleshooting section mapping common errors (image pull backoff, auth failures) to missing endpoints.

## Open questions
- Do we mandate CW Logs endpoint for all alpha deployments even when customers prefer alternate sinks (e.g., Splunk via forwarder)? Current decision: require by default, allow explicit opt-out.
- Do we add KMS as “required when encryption is enabled” in a future beta/GA scope?
